A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all pages, including appendices, are readable. The substantive difference is confined to Appendix F.2; rendered pages 2–30 are identical.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations across translation, summarization and peer review, including discrimination scores, model ablations and adversarial attacks (Tables 2–7).

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical evaluations and results in Tables 2–7 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The mutual-evaluation game, information-based scoring, TVD-MI critic and inference procedures in Sections 3.1–3.4 remain unchanged. The appended proof does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two translation datasets, seven summarization datasets and ICLR peer-review data, with unchanged agent strategies and attack scenarios.

E2.justification: MI (DoE), GPPM, judges with and without references, ROUGE/BLEU and the Table 3 embedding baseline retain the same participation in corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Sample counts, model configurations, evaluation metrics, aggregation procedures and attack implementations are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A and C–E.

E4.justification: The model ablation, four adversarial transformations, compression/effective-rank analyses and evaluation-inversion case studies remain unchanged (Tables 3, 5–7; Figure 2).

E5.justification: Confidence intervals, 10,000 bootstrap iterations for AUC, significance reporting and multiple-testing adjustments are unchanged. The new probability bounds belong to a theoretical proof, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings and empirical findings in Tables 2–7 and Figure 2 are identical. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v3 contains a main-text proof sketch and the Lemma F.1 proof, but its appendix ends after restating Theorem 3.3. v4 adds a detailed proof argument in Appendix F.2: a finite-support surrogate construction, coupling, collision bounds in equations (5)–(6), and derivation of the 1−δ−1/k probability guarantee. This substantially expands the formal argument for a central theorem without changing its statement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about information-based evaluation, certification limits, item-level detection and adversarial robustness. The added proof does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of robustness and compression, and limitations concerning adaptive overlap attacks, extreme compression and dependence on pretrained knowledge, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation configurations, temperatures, token limits, prompts, computational resource disclosures and code/pre-registration access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, including the positioning relative to McAllester and Stratos and earlier peer-prediction methods.

P1.justification: Appendix F.2 gains localized proof prose, replacing the stray 'd' after the theorem. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added proof slightly reflows page 31 and introduces a piecewise distribution and displayed probability bounds extending onto page 32. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–10 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the intended proof more explicit than v3's sketch and unfinished Appendix F.2. However, page 32 asserts that absence of repeated tail pairs ensures equal empirical joint types; Definition 3.2 also preserves row/column overlap, which distinct pairs alone do not guarantee. The addition therefore does not clearly close the theoretical gap. With the empirical evidence unchanged, its transparency benefit does not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
